# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Nigeria, 2024: 3B.2 research note

**Bottom line:** The record is **mostly negative**. Tinubu publicly endorsed police professionalism and later ordered the release of detained minors, but there is **no clear evidence** he punished abusive officers or meaningfully restrained the security apparatus during the protest crackdown. The strongest 2024 evidence points to **tolerated abuse, excessive force, and punitive escalation**.

## Accepted claims

- [We Will Transform Nigeria Police Into Modern, Professional Force – President Tinubu](/statehouse.gov.ng/we-will-transform-nigeria-police-into-modern-professional-force-president-tinubu/) — State House, Abuja, April 16, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu said his administration was reforming the police to be modern, professional, accountable, and better trained. This is the clearest positive evidence, but it is aspirational rather than proof that abuse was actually prevented or punished. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](/statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) — State House, Abuja, August 4, 2024. Claim summary: Tinubu acknowledged deaths, destruction, and unrest, and told law enforcement to protect lives and property responsibly. This is partial restraint language, but it does not show concrete discipline of abusive units. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`, `1B.8`

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](/www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) — Reuters via Investing.com, July 31, 2024. Claim summary: Reuters reported the government said it was open to dialogue even as security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence: some de-escalatory posture, but no sign of disciplining the forces that would later use abuse. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`, `1B.8`

- [At least 3 killed in Nigeria at protests over high cost of living](/www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376) — Reuters via Investing.com, August 1, 2024. Claim summary: Reuters reported at least three protesters were killed in Kaduna during nationwide demonstrations. This is direct evidence of lethal force under Tinubu’s watch and weak evidence of restraint or accountability. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests](/www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) — Amnesty International, November 28, 2024. Claim summary: Amnesty said police used live ammunition, killed at least 24 people, detained more than 1,200, and tortured at least one detainee. It also said the authorities denied wrongdoing despite evidence. This is the strongest evidence that abuse was tolerated rather than prevented. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- [Nigeria: Protesters Charged with Treason](/www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) — Human Rights Watch, September 6, 2024. Claim summary: HRW said authorities charged protesters with treason, kept them in custody with limited access to lawyers, and held minors in conditions raising humane-treatment concerns. This supports a finding of tolerated abusive policing and punitive political imprisonment. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- [Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests](/www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000) — Reuters via Investing.com, November 1, 2024. Claim summary: Reuters reported the government expanded treason charges to 76 people, including minors, after the protests. This suggests continued tolerance of exemplary punishment rather than correction of earlier abuses. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`

- [Tinubu orders release of minors arrested during EndBadGovernance protests](/www.icirnigeria.org/tinubu-orders-release-of-minors-arrested-during-endbadgovernance-protests/) — ICIR Nigeria, November 4, 2024. Claim summary: After public outrage, Tinubu ordered the release of minors detained over the protests. This is the clearest corrective action in the record, but it came after the abuse and does not show broader punishment of abusive officers. Question IDs: `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`

## Synthesis

For **3B.2**, the best-supported reading is:

- **Some positive signals:** police-reform language and the late release of minors.
- **Dominant negative pattern:** lethal protest policing, excessive force, treason charges, and no visible punishment of abusive officers.
- **Net:** Tinubu appears to have **tolerated abuse more than he prevented or punished it**.

## Search gap

- I found **no direct evidence** of discipline against abusive police, military, intelligence, prison, militia, party-enforcer, or vigilante actors.
- I also found **no specific evidence** of accountability measures against senior officials responsible for the protest crackdown.
